node.title: Re: Should I use carp/croak or warn/die
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Note that [doc://Carp] doesn't automatically include a stack trace, that's only if you do perl -MCarp=verbose script.pl or $Carp::Verbose=1;, or you explicitly use confess. I like to use [doc://Carp] in my modules because it reports the error as coming from the user's code, rather than the module itself, which makes more sense for many error cases (like incorrect parameters). When it's an internal error that I don't expect the user to see (at least not often), I'll sometimes use confess to get the full stack trace.

$ cat Foo.pm package Foo; use warnings; use strict; use Carp; sub one { die "Bad call to one"; } sub two { carp "Bad call to two"; } sub three { confess "Some error in three"; } 1; $ perl -I. -MFoo -le 'Foo::one' Bad call to one at Foo.pm line 5. $ perl -I. -MFoo -le 'Foo::two' Bad call to two at -e line 1. $ perl -I. -MFoo -le 'Foo::three' Some error in three at Foo.pm line 7. Foo::three() called at -e line 1
